title: Grant applications, splash pads and Sunview apartment approval
subtitle: Regional speed cameras, affordable housing grants, 2024 budget projection, skating club and Air Force lease, Woolwich Street townhouse meeting
overview: Council approved two applications to the provincial Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund: one for accessibility and cooling upgrades at the Albert McCormick Community Centre arenas, the other for expanded ball diamonds at RIM Park. The City's share is committed only if the grants succeed {{vote:m4}}. Council also awarded the contract for two splash pads with washroom buildings {{vote:m9}}.

Council adopted Official Plan Amendment 51 and approved the rezoning for a 13-storey, 131-unit apartment building at 249-253 Sunview Street {{vote:m10}}. It also approved new licence and lease agreements with the Kitchener-Waterloo Skating Club {{vote:m6}} and the Royal Canadian Air Force Association wing {{vote:m5}}. Staff reported a projected 2024 tax-base surplus of about $0.8 million and an enterprise deficit of about $1.1 million {{vote:m8}}.

Council heard a Region presentation on its municipal speed camera program and received the first round of affordable rental housing grants for information {{vote:m7}}. An informal public meeting on an 11-unit townhouse proposal on Woolwich Street drew many resident concerns. No decision was made on that application. After a closed session, the minutes record no public decisions.

decisions.detail: Council approved applications for the AMCC revitalization and accessibility retrofit and the RIM Park Diamonds 4, 5 and 6 expansion, with City matching funds if successful and signing authority for the transfer agreement.
Council adopted Official Plan Amendment 51, asked the Region to approve it, and approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-24-02 for 249-253 Sunview Street.

decisions.item: Splash pads and washroom buildings contract
decisions.detail: Council awarded RFT24-20 to Yard Weasels Inc. for a total of $1,547,957.86 and approved $150,000 in project transfers.
Council acknowledged a projected tax-base surplus of about $0.8 million and an enterprise deficit of about $1.1 million, and asked staff for a final allocation report by May 2025.
Council approved a 2025-2028 licence agreement with the Kitchener-Waterloo Skating Club for space at RIM Park Manulife Sportsplex.
Council approved a lease for 404 K-W Wing (Royal Canadian Air Force Association) at 510 Dutton Dr.
Council received for information the report on the first round of grant recipients under the affordable rental housing program.

debate: On the recreation grants, one councillor asked whether cooling systems for the AMCC arenas could still be added if the grant failed. Staff said they see cooling as important, including for use as a cooling centre, and would look to existing budgets.

On the housing grants, councillors asked why the next intake waits until spring and whether the co-op study would address financing hurdles. Staff said they must first finish agreements for the two awards. They said the study is meant to support a later submission to the federal housing agency.

At the Woolwich Street townhouse meeting, residents raised tree removal, traffic, on-street parking, snow storage, drainage and grading, infrastructure capacity and the loss of current rental homes. Some said notice was too short. The applicant's planner said the team would consider more tree planting and keep talking with residents.
Councillors asked about site plan oversight for the Woolwich Street project, which could fall below the 10-unit threshold. Staff said conditions could be explored through a later consent application.

On Sunview Street, councillors asked about low parking and all one-bedroom units. Staff said provincial changes removed parking minimums near transit. The applicant's planner said combining units would exceed the density limit.
